name: Bear Call Diagonal Spread (Short Call Diagonal, Credit)
summary: Sell a shorter-dated lower-strike call and buy a longer-dated higher-strike call; a credit diagonal that is a bear call spread with extra time bought on the protective leg.

legs.strike_rule: Lower strike by delta 0.20-0.35 (OTM above spot).

Higher strike, width 1-5 points above the short depending on the underlying's price; choose the width so that (width x 100 - credit) <= 1.5% of equity. Protective leg is bought in a LATER expiry, which is what makes this a diagonal rather than a vertical.
legs.dte_rule: back expiry, at least 21 days beyond the front, typically 45-90 DTE

max_profit: The net credit received PLUS the residual value of the long back-month call after the short expires worthless. Unlike a vertical, the long leg survives and can be sold or reused.
max_loss: (Long strike - short strike) x 100 - net credit, at front expiry. Note this understates the true max only if the long is closed before the short, which the rules forbid.
breakevens: Approximately short strike + (credit + residual long value)/100 at front expiry; wider than the equivalent vertical because the long leg retains value.

greeks.delta: net negative, roughly -0.10 to -0.25 per unit
greeks.theta: positive while spot is below the short strike
greeks.vega: net positive or near flat - the back-month long's vega partially or fully offsets the short's, which makes this less vol-sensitive than a plain bear call spread

when_to_use: IV rank 35-70 (you want to sell a rich front-month call) combined with a downtrend or a resistance rejection. The diagonal version is preferable to a plain vertical when back-month vol is cheap relative to front (backwardation), because you buy your protection in the cheaper month and it outlives the short.
entry_rules: Trend/level filter: spot < 50-day SMA, or spot has just been rejected at a resistance level within 2 sessions.
Short call by delta 0.20-0.35; long call strike above it; long expiry at least 21 days beyond the short expiry.
Credit >= 25% of the strike width (e.g. >= $0.25 on a $1 wide, >= $1.25 on a $5 wide).
Max loss (width x 100 - credit) <= 1.5% of equity per unit.
LEVEL 3 OK: the short call is covered by a higher-strike long call with a LATER expiry. The requirement is width-based, not debit-based. Submit as a 2-leg mleg; if legging, buy the long call FIRST.
management_rules: Take profit at 50% of the credit received (close the short, and decide separately on the long).
Stop at 2x the credit received as a loss, or when the short call's |delta| reaches 0.50.
Close or roll at 21 DTE on the short leg regardless of P&L if the short's delta is above 0.35.
Roll the short up and out for a credit only; never roll into an expiry beyond the long leg's expiry.
If the long back-month call is worth more than 40% of the max loss and the thesis has flipped bullish, keep the long after buying back the short - it is a free directional option.
Max 3 units per underlying; aggregate credit-diagonal max loss <= 10% of equity.
exit_rules: Close or roll the short call by 14:30 ET on its expiration day, unconditionally.
Close the short call immediately if extrinsic <= $0.05/share or |delta| >= 0.90.
Close the short call before the session preceding ex-dividend if extrinsic < dividend per share.
NEVER close the long leg while the short is open - that converts the trade into a naked short call. The long may only be sold after the short is bought back.
If the short is deep ITM and spot is above the long strike, close both legs as a package; do not attempt to salvage.
assignment_risk: Only the short front-month call. Assignment delivers -100 shares, covered by a long call at a HIGHER strike in a later expiry - so the cover is real but imperfect: the shares are short from the lower strike and the call only caps risk above the higher strike. Flatten the stock within one session. Ex-dividend is the dominant early-assignment trigger.
buying_power: (Long strike - short strike) x 100 minus the net credit, held as maintenance for the life of the short. Alpaca treats the later-expiring higher-strike long as valid cover for level 3.
liquidity_needs: Both expiries OI >= 300; the short expiry should be penny or nickel wide. Underlying ADV >= 2M shares.
common_mistakes: Closing the long leg first to 'save a commission' and creating a naked short call; buying the long in an expiry that is only a week later, so it provides almost no residual value; rolling the short past the long's expiry, which un-covers the position; treating it as a vertical for margin purposes.
zero_dte_notes: Not under this playbook; the short's minimum DTE at entry is 21.
family: Calendar and diagonal spreads (time spreads): same-strike calendars, different-strike diagonals, double/triple calendars, double diagonals, PMCC and its put mirror, LEAPS diagonals, calendarized straddles/butterflies, ratio time spreads, and the reverse (short) time spreads
